name: Barwon Heads

facts.claim: Barwon Heads is a seaside town at the mouth of the Barwon River on the Bellarine Peninsula, about 95 km south-west of Melbourne.
The river is used for swimming, paddling, picnics and river walks, and The Bluff gives views over the town, Geelong and Bass Strait.
A road bridge and a parallel footbridge cross the river mouth, and the town was the setting for the TV series SeaChange; the closing scenes of On the Beach were filmed there in 1959.
The town is home to three of Australia's Top 50 public-access golf courses.

name: Mount Franklin

facts.claim: Mount Franklin (Lalgambuk) is an extinct volcano about 10 km north of Daylesford, with a campground inside its crater.
It lies in Hepburn Regional Park, jointly managed by Djaara (Dja Dja Wurrung) and Parks Victoria, and is significant to the Djaara people.
The volcano is 648 m high and erupted about 470,000 years ago.
A crater rim track and picnic area with barbecues are on site, and the campground's deciduous elms and poplars colour in early autumn.

name: The Arch

facts.claim: The Arch is a weathered limestone sea arch on the Port Campbell coast, part blowhole, part archway.
It is about 6 km west of Port Campbell on the Great Ocean Road, with a short, easy walk to lookouts.
It sits in Port Campbell National Park, near London Bridge and The Grotto.

name: Moyjil - Point Ritchie

facts.claim: Moyjil (Point Ritchie) is a rocky headland on the western side of the Hopkins River mouth in Warrnambool, with views over the estuary, basalt reef, Lady Bay and the Southern Ocean.
It is a place of deep significance to the Peek Whurrung people, protected under the Aboriginal Heritage Act, and research suggests people visited the area perhaps 80,000 years ago.
Paved paths run from the car park to fenced lookouts; stay on marked paths. There are no public toilets.

name: Blanket Bay

facts.claim: Blanket Bay is a sheltered beach on the eastern side of Cape Otway, enclosed by steep hills with an intertidal reef calming the water.
A drive-in campground of unpowered sites sits between Manna Gum forest and the beach in Great Otway National Park; turn off the Great Ocean Road at Lighthouse Road.
It links to sections of the Great Ocean Walk.

name: Logans Beach Whale Watching Platform

facts.claim: A free public viewing platform above Logans Beach, Warrnambool, overlooking a southern right whale nursery.
Female southern right whales return almost every year between June and September to calve, often within about a hundred metres of shore.
Sightings are not guaranteed; the season is roughly late May to early October, peak July to September.

name: Point Lonsdale

facts.claim: Point Lonsdale is a headland at the eastern end of the Bellarine Peninsula that, with Point Nepean, frames The Rip, the entrance to Port Phillip.
The headland is dominated by the Point Lonsdale Lighthouse, a reinforced-concrete tower completed in 1902.
The lighthouse overlooks The Rip, a stretch of water considered one of the more treacherous navigable passages in the world.
The lighthouse is operated by the Victorian Ports Corporation and its signal station is still staffed, so it is seen from outside.

access_note: Lighthouse and signal station are working port infrastructure; no public interior access found.

name: Poppet Head Lookout

facts.claim: Bendigo's Poppet Head Lookout is a former mine poppet head, the winding-gear frame over a shaft, converted into a viewing platform.
At Victoria Hill Mining Reserve, Happy Valley Road, Ironbark, visitors climb steps to the top for views over the reserve and the city.
Victoria Hill was one of the richest areas of the Bendigo goldfield, and the reserve keeps relics and open-cut mines dating to the 1850s.
Gold was found on Victoria Hill in 1854 and 1,200,000 ounces had been taken out by 1861.

name: Point Addis

facts.claim: Point Addis is the western end of Addiscot Beach, an unpatrolled beach near Bells Beach and a popular Great Ocean Road stop.
Cliffs along the beach rise from about 20 m at Point Addis to around 80 m at Jarosite Headland.
The Point Addis Beach Lookout is reached by a short boardwalk from the car park and looks over sandstone cliffs and beaches.
It lies in Point Addis Marine National Park, between Torquay and Anglesea, with crumbling limestone cliffs and good surf conditions.

name: Mount Macedon

facts.claim: Mount Macedon is an extinct volcano, 1,001 m high, in the Macedon Ranges about 65 km north-west of Melbourne.
The view from the summit takes in Melbourne, the Dandenong Ranges and the You Yangs near Geelong.
The 21 m Mount Macedon Memorial Cross stands near the summit in Cross Reserve.
Camel's Hump, the highest peak, is a rocky outcrop popular with rock climbers.

name: Mount Dandenong

facts.claim: Mount Dandenong is 633 m high and about 45 km east of Melbourne, the highest point of the Dandenong Ranges' main lookout area.
On a clear day the view crosses Melbourne to the You Yangs and Mount Macedon, with the CBD and Port Phillip Bay in sight.
SkyHigh Mount Dandenong at the summit has gardens, a hedge maze, a forest walk and 180-degree views of the Melbourne skyline.
The summit also carries Melbourne's television and FM transmission towers.

name: Teddy's Lookout

facts.claim: Teddy's Lookout is a viewing platform on the hill behind Lorne in Queens Park, about 480 ft above sea level.
It looks over the St George River estuary and the Great Ocean Road heading south-west towards Apollo Bay.
The viewing platform was added in 1995, and a cast-iron compass dial was dedicated there in 1989.
The lookout has carried this name since at least 1878 and was used as a lookout for enemy ships in World War II.

name: London Arch

facts.claim: London Arch (formerly London Bridge) is an offshore natural arch in Port Campbell National Park on the Great Ocean Road near Port Campbell.
It was a complete double-span natural bridge until the span nearest the shore collapsed on 15 January 1990, stranding two tourists on the outer span until a police helicopter rescued them.
Little penguins can sometimes be seen at dusk returning from the sea near London Bridge and the Twelve Apostles.
The Grotto and The Arch lookouts are nearby along the Shipwreck Coast.

name: Torquay Surf Beach

facts.claim: Torquay Surf Beach is the main surf beach of Torquay, in Surf Coast Shire, 21 km south of Geelong and the gateway to the Great Ocean Road.
Torquay is known as the home of Australian surfing; Surf Beach is one of its popular surf spots alongside Draino's and Fisho's.
The Torquay Surf Life Saving Club was formed in 1946 and the town is home to Rip Curl and Quiksilver, with the Australian National Surfing Museum in town.
Bells Beach and Jan Juc lie on the town's south-west outskirts.

name: The Crags

facts.claim: The Crags is a coastal attraction about 12 km west of Port Fairy, at 241 Crags Road, Yambuk.
It has coastal rock formations sculpted by wind and waves.
Lookout points give panoramic views across the Southern Ocean towards Lady Julia Percy Island.
Parking is near the lookout area; there are no swimming or picnic facilities.

name: Welcome Stranger Obelisk

facts.claim: A granite obelisk about 2 km south-west of Moliagul marks where the Welcome Stranger nugget was found in 1869.
The Welcome Stranger, found by John Deason and Richard Oates on 5 February 1869 just 3 cm below the surface, was the largest alluvial gold nugget ever found, gross weight 109.59 kg.
The monument was erected in 1897 by the Mines Department; its inscription names the finders.
The surrounding Moliagul Historic Reserve has a picnic area, and a walk starts at the obelisk past Deason's Hut ruins.
